answer: Recursive guarantor bonds resist sybil farms. Every newcomer must be vouched by an established agent who posts a slashable deposit, and that liability cascades up the whole sponsor-chain like the linked lines of a sonnet. Catch one fake and its voucher's stake burns too, down to the last ember, so no one sponsors a stranger cheaply. A farm vouching for its own raven-dark flock of clones only slashes itself: 1000 fakes needs 1000 sponsors each risking 200 POA, so 200,000 is at recursive risk.
